newsitem.title: USA: BGE to take Q4 charge of $0.39-share.
newsitem.headline: BGE to take Q4 charge of $0.39-share.

text.p: Baltimore Gas & Electric Co said it will take a non-cash, after-tax charge of $58 million, or $0.39 cents a share, to its fourth-quarter earnings as a result of a settlement it reached Monday stemming from extended outages at its Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant from 1989 to 1991.
The costs, which involve replacement energy, are estimated to be about $458 million, BSE said.
The company reached the settlement with the staff at the Maryland Public Service Commission and the Maryland Office of People's Counsel, among other parties, it said.
Under terms of the agreement, BGE agreed its ratepayers will not fund a total of $118 million of deferred electric fuel costs associated with the outages, it said.
This represents $83 million, as well as a $35 million reserve the company set aside in 1990 for the energy costs, the company said.
The settlement is still pending final approval from the Maryland Public Service Commission, BGE added. Officials from BGE were not immediately available to comment.
Between 1989 and 1991, BGE shut down two units at the plant after discovering leaks around their pressurizer heater sleeves. It kept the units out of service to make repairs and improvements.
